name: Dev Ecosystem Dashboard
tag: Sets up rules, skills, guardrail hooks, subagents and plugins so your coding agents work your way.

scenarios.title: Set up a team repo for agents
scenarios.ask: Set up our main repo for coding agents. {devs} developers, {lang}, with {strict} guardrails.
steps: Wrote a project rules file: build and test commands, folder layout and code style for {lang}.
Added 4 skills: write a migration, add an API route, update the changelog, release notes.
Installed {=strict * 2 + 1} guardrail hooks, such as blocking edits to secrets files and running the linter before commits.
Created a Test writer and a Reviewer subagent with read-only access to production configs.
Bundled everything as one plugin so all {devs} developers get the same setup.
followups: What does a guardrail hook do?
It runs before or after an agent action. For example, it can stop the agent from editing files that hold secrets, or run tests after every change.
Update the plugin once. Developers get the new version the next time they start a session.

scenarios.title: Stop agents breaking the build
scenarios.ask: Agent changes broke the main build {breaks} times last month. Add hooks to catch this earlier.

inputs.label: Test suite run time in minutes

steps: Matched {breaks} breaks to their causes: type errors, missing imports and a skipped migration.
Added a post-edit hook for type checks and a pre-commit hook that runs fast tests.
Added a rule: always run the migration check when touching the schema folder.
Estimated how many breaks the new hooks would have caught.

result.title: Guardrails added
rows: Breaks that would have been caught

followups: Won't hooks slow the agent down?
A little. The pre-commit hook runs only fast tests, capped at a few minutes, and the full suite stays in CI.
Can developers turn a hook off?
Admins choose which hooks are required and which developers can switch off locally.

scenarios.title: Audit installed plugins
scenarios.ask: Our developers installed {plugins} plugins and {servers} MCP servers. Which ones are risky?
steps: Listed {plugins} plugins and {servers} MCP servers across all machines.
Found {=max(1, round((plugins + servers) * 0.15))} with write access to files outside the repo.
Drafted an allow-list. Nothing is removed until an admin approves.
followups: Why do MCP servers need checking?
A server can give the agent new abilities, like reading files or calling services. Knowing who made it and what it can touch matters.
Yes. With the allow-list on, new plugins outside the list need an admin's approval.
